definition: Updating a model continuously as new data arrives, as opposed to batch training on a fixed dataset.
details: Updating a model continuously as new data arrives, as opposed to batch training on a fixed dataset. Relevant to recommendation systems, fraud detection, and any setting with rapid distribution shift.

explainer.lead: Online learning updates a model continuously as new data arrives rather than training once on a fixed dataset. It matters where data distributions shift quickly.

tiers.eli5: It is like adjusting your route while driving as traffic changes, instead of planning once before leaving.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it for recommendation systems, fraud detection and any setting with rapid distribution shift. The usual pitfall is instability when updates are noisy or poorly paced.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as continuous updating as new data arrives, in contrast to batch training on a fixed dataset. Limits: behaviour depends on the stream; the given material names none specifically.

explainer.example: A fraud detector updates its model as each new transaction arrives.
